title: The Boy Who Came Out of the Forest

pages.text: Appiagyei went to gather firewood at the edge of the forest with his cousin. He paused to admire a bright blue bird. When he looked around, his cousin was gone, and every tree looked the same.
sentences: Appiagyei went to gather firewood at the edge of the forest with his cousin.
He paused to admire a bright blue bird.
When he looked around, his cousin was gone, and every tree looked the same.
pages.alt: Appiagyei standing alone among tall green forest-edge trees with a small bundle of twigs, looking up at a vivid blue bird on a branch.

pages.text: Appiagyei remembered what his teacher had taught the class: “If you are lost, stop. Do not run in circles.” He sat down beside the wide roots of a giant silk-cotton tree and took a slow, deep breath.
sentences: Appiagyei remembered what his teacher had taught the class: “If you are lost, stop.
Do not run in circles.” He sat down beside the wide roots of a giant silk-cotton tree and took a slow, deep breath.
pages.alt: Appiagyei sitting calmly against the buttress roots of a huge forest tree with his hands on his knees, breathing steadily.

pages.text: He called out and blew the red whistle his mother had given him for farm trips. He blew three short blasts, again and again. He did not drink from any pool or eat strange berries. He stayed right by the big tree.
sentences: He called out and blew the red whistle his mother had given him for farm trips.
He blew three short blasts, again and again.
He did not drink from any pool or eat strange berries.
He stayed right by the big tree.
pages.alt: Appiagyei standing beside the same giant tree trunk blowing his bright red neck-whistle in late afternoon light, ignoring wild red berries on a nearby bush.

pages.text: Night fell, and the air grew cool. He tucked dry leaves around his legs and stayed calm. The dark forest was full of sounds, yet they were only tree frogs, crickets, and an owl high overhead.
sentences: Night fell, and the air grew cool.
He tucked dry leaves around his legs and stayed calm.
The dark forest was full of sounds, yet they were only tree frogs, crickets, and an owl high overhead.
pages.alt: Under a starry indigo sky, Appiagyei sitting bravely among dry leaves against the giant tree, while an owl perches peacefully on a high branch and a tiny green frog sits on a leaf.

pages.text: At dawn, the village searchers heard his whistle. “Over here!” he called. They found him tired and thirsty, yet safe and unharmed. His mother held him tight for a long time.
sentences: At dawn, the village searchers heard his whistle.
They found him tired and thirsty, yet safe and unharmed.
His mother held him tight for a long time.
pages.alt: In golden early-morning light by the giant tree, Appiagyei’s mother kneels to hug him tightly while relieved village searchers with hand torches smile nearby.

pages.text: Some elders said the little people of the forest had watched over him. Others said he stayed safe because he kept calm and used his whistle. Nobody knew for sure, yet everyone agreed: stop, blow your whistle, stay put, and always tell a grown-up where you are going.
sentences: Some elders said the little people of the forest had watched over him.
Others said he stayed safe because he kept calm and used his whistle.
Nobody knew for sure, yet everyone agreed: stop, blow your whistle, stay put, and always tell a grown-up where you are going.
pages.alt: Back at the sunlit village compound, elders and neighbours gather warmly around Appiagyei and his mother while he holds a cup of clean water.

activities.question: What does Appiagyei do first when he realises he is lost?
What do the villagers say about how he stayed safe?
options: They all agree it was magic
They all say it was luck

items: Appiagyei loses sight of his cousin.
He sits by a big tree and stays calm.
He blows his whistle in sets of three.
The searchers find him at dawn.

activities.prompt: How would you feel if you were lost and then found safely?

glossary.definition: A small tube you blow into to make a clear, loud sound.
People working together to find someone who is lost.
